key_insight: A classifier chain model can predict likely pathology tests from patient symptoms before physician consultation, improving test recommendation speed and accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This could support faster, more consistent diagnostic planning by reducing reliance on subjective test selection and helping clinicians prioritize appropriate tests.
method: Framed test recommendation as a multi-label classification problem.
Compared Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and ensemble approaches using Classifier Chain.
Used SHAP to explain which symptoms influenced each test recommendation.
evidence_signal: On the SOUTHERN.IML pathology dataset plus an expert-built custom dataset, Logistic Regression with Classifier Chain achieved 98.83% accuracy, while Majority Voting had the best balance of precision (0.93), recall (0.85), and F1-score (0.89).
watch_item: The model appears to be based on a specific dataset and expert-labeled custom data, so external validation and real-world clinical workflow testing would be important before implementation.
